main.description: A way of playing a poem back. Anyone may publish a rendering of anyone's poem; the original record is never touched and its strong reference still resolves. This is how a poem gets covered, arranged, and argued with.

renderer.description: Which engine draws the track. Omit for the built-in text player. A client that does not recognise the renderer ignores it and falls back to the built-in one, so a rendering is never unplayable.

recipe.description: Every parameter, as a query string. A few keys are read by the player itself (timing, grid, fade, del, sound, and the four colours); the rest belong to the renderer and are opaque here. Same serialisation Titivillus and SIGNGULARITY already use for shareable links. Data, never code.

recipeBlob.description: For recipes too large to inline.

name.description: What to call this treatment. Two renderings sharing a renderer and recipe are the same treatment whether or not they share a name.

note.description: Why this poem was rendered this way.
